diagnostics.notation_map: Per (layer, KV-head): the memory's weight matrix is W = V_S^T (d x t), its KEY is the routing vector a_S(q) = softmax(qK^T/sqrt(d)+beta)_S in R^t_{>=0} (literally X at value_solve.py:86), and the old-key second moment is C0 = A_old^T A_old (t x t). Non-negative keys imply <a_old,a_new> >= 0 always, so two routing vectors are orthogonal iff their supports are disjoint.

command: No code executed on GPU and no source file modified. Files edited: research_loop/state/literature_ledger.md (append-only, 3 Edit calls appending LIT-009..LIT-018 after LIT-008) and this bundle. NOTE: `git status` shows cartridges/am/{continual,finetune,value_solve}.py and examples/qasper2/train/continual_am_sparse.py as modified - those are the in-flight ORACLE-WRITE worker's edits, NOT mine. Sources read: AlphaEdit arXiv 2410.02355 (+ reproducibility study 2606.26783), MEMIT arXiv 2210.07229, EMMET/ROME arXiv 2403.14236, Adam-NSCL CVPR 2021, OWM Nature MI 2019, GPM arXiv 2103.09762, Schlag et al. arXiv 2102.11174, DeltaNet arXiv 2406.06484, test-time regression arXiv 2501.12352, Larimar arXiv 2403.11901, modern Hopfield arXiv 2008.02217, covariance-trap critique arXiv 2603.15518.
observations: Ten entries written, LIT-009..LIT-018, all with a prediction about one of our measured signatures; none marked unusable. The single most consequential finding is a code fact, not a paper fact: our canonical write is ALREADY the MEMIT update, with the wrong metric. continual_am_sparse.py:96 sets DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2 (overriding the 0.0 dataclass default), so finetune.py:580 sent every AM run in results.csv through guarded_sparse_am_value_update, which minimises ||A_new V_S - R_new||^2 + w||V_S - V_S_old||^2 - exactly MEMIT's Delta = R K1^T (C0 + K1 K1^T)^-1 with C0 = w*I. The entire editing literature (MEMIT, EMMET, AlphaEdit, Adam-NSCL, OWM, GPM, Larimar) is then one statement: C0 should be the second moment of the OLD keys, not the identity. Under the correct mapping our 'key' is the simplex-valued routing vector a_S(q) = alpha[:, S] (literally X at value_solve.py:86), not the model's key vector, so C0 = A_old^T A_old is a t x t routing Gram collectable in one QA forward pass with hooks we already have. Second finding: three independent literatures converge on the same statement of B-ROUTE. Test-time regression (arXiv 2501.12352) shows softmax attention is NONPARAMETRIC (Nadaraya-Watson), so a new association requires a new key - there is no parametric weight to fold it into; modern Hopfield (arXiv 2008.02217) says retrievability is set by key separation Delta_i and poorly separated keys yield metastable averages; and the fast-weight literature (arXiv 2102.11174) says interference is governed by key overlap and capacity by the number of orthogonal keys. All three imply the same hard bound, and it is a quantity our code already computes and no bundle has ever recorded: mass_on_S (value_solve.py:146, finetune.py:628). Third finding: null-space value editing cannot work at our current support. With top_t=64 and n_old >> 64, C0 in R^{64x64} is generically full rank, so AlphaEdit's projector P is zero and the update vanishes; null-space editing is only defined for us at large top_t (up to 512) where the QA routing Gram can be rank-deficient. That makes it a reason to revisit support size - the setting SCOUT-AM already re-opened for a different reason (query count) - rather than a drop-in. Fourth: preconditioning and projection are RETENTION mechanisms and cannot by themselves move MT; our QA is already 0.34 ahead of its budget (2.177 vs 2.52), so their value is that they convert retention slack into support/plasticity. Fifth: Larimar (arXiv 2403.11901) is the closest published system - frozen LLM, fixed 512-slot memory, one-shot closed-form pseudo-inverse write, RLS sequential update C_i = C_{i-1} + a_i W_i^T W_i, M_i = M_{i-1} + a_i C_i^-1 W_i^T (Z_i - W_i M_{i-1}), with alpha=-1 as exact erasure - and it reports ~100% fidelity at 512 edits into 512 slots, i.e. about one write per slot; we ask 64 shared slots to absorb many documents. Caveats on all of the above: every prediction is untested here, the AlphaEdit reproducibility study (arXiv 2606.26783) measured that null-space protection is 'bounded rather than unconditional' whenever the linear-contribution assumption breaks (it failed outright on Gemma2 due to post-FFN layernorm), and our path from V to CE is far less linear than any FFN edit; the covariance-trap critique (arXiv 2603.15518) argues MEMIT-C0 and AlphaEdit-P are geometrically equivalent and both marginal, which LIT-018 turns into a falsifiable three-arm control. RANKING (findings, not a recommendation). By expected movement on MT below 2.0 while holding QA <= 2.52: (1) LIT-017, null-space KEY placement - the only imported/synthesised operator that attacks acquisition (routing) and retention with one construction, and the only one that escapes the nonparametric bound of LIT-014/LIT-016, since it gives MT queries a key to route to; it is also the mechanism AM.pdf S6 explicitly leaves open, it costs 288 tiny 128x128 EVDs and ~19 MB, and it runs through the already-wired but never-tested key_mode != 'freeze' branch. Its dependency is that beta must work first (B-SOLVE), because orthogonality sets a QA logit of 0, not -infinity. (2) LIT-011 + LIT-012, null-space value projection at LARGE top_t - not an acquisition mechanism on its own, but the only way to spend our 0.34 of QA slack on support without paying EXP-007's monotone QA cost; a single tau sweep traces the whole Pareto front between the Phase-1 floor (QA 2.2388 / MT 3.7826) and today's point. (3) LIT-009/LIT-010, C0-metric solve - one-line changes at core.py:208 and core.py:198-204 respectively, sharing one statistic; LIT-010 additionally predicts a SIGN FLIP on the board's unexplained EXP-007 top128 anomaly, since that arm is precisely the identity-metric min-norm interpolant EMMET says should be taken in the C0^-1 metric. (4) LIT-013/LIT-015, disjoint-support slot selection and per-document capacity - cheap, and they reinterpret the refuted K-GATE result as 'IDF was the wrong orthogonality proxy' rather than 'orthogonality does not matter'. CHEAPEST DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT for the whole block: one no-training diagnostic over a Phase-1 cartridge that computes, per (layer, KV-head), (a) the eigenspectrum and effective rank of the QA routing Gram C0 = sum a_QA a_QA^T at top_t=512, (b) rho = E_{q in MT} ||P a(q)||^2 / ||a(q)||^2, the MT routing energy lying in C0's approximate null space, (c) mass_on_S for MT vs QA reference queries at top_t in {32,64,128} plus the routing entropies H(a_MT), H(a_QA), and (d) the overlap sum_j min(abar_QA,j, abar_MT,j). Those four numbers jointly decide the block: rho near 0 or overlap large refutes LIT-011/012/013 at once and confirms B-ROUTE as capped independently of the write-ceiling oracle; mass_on_S far below t/512 bounds every value-only mechanism; a fast-decaying C0 spectrum is the precondition without which null-space editing is identically zero at any support we have run. It needs forward passes only - no solve, no training, no gradient - and it reuses install_query_capture_hooks and compute_attention_weights unchanged.
